Proposition
[Scalar maximum principle, third version] Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0108 1. Proposition 4.3\group weak-maximum-principles-scalar-equations

Let $u : \mathcal M^n imes [0,T) o \mathbb R$ be a $C^2$ supersolution to \[ rac{\partial v}{\partial t} = \Delta _{g(t)} v + \langle X, abla v angle + eta v \] on a closed manifold. Suppose that for each $ au \in [0,T)$ there exists $C_ au <\infty $ such that $ eta (x,t)\le C_ au $ for all $x \in \mathcal M^n$ and $t \in [0, au ]$. If $u(x,0)\ge 0$ for all $x \in \mathcal M^n$, then $u(x,t)\ge 0$ for all $x \in \mathcal M^n$ and $t \in [0,T)$.

Proof

Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0108 \sketch For a fixed $ au \in (0,T)$, set

\[ J(x,t)\doteq e^{-C_ au t}u(x,t). \]

Then

\[ rac{\partial J}{\partial t}\ge \Delta _{g(t)}J+\langle X, abla J angle +( eta -C_ au )J. \]

Since $ eta -C_ au \le 0$ on $\mathcal M^n imes [0, au ]$, the function $J$ is a supersolution of the heat equation at points where $J\le 0$. By Theorem 1, $J\ge 0$ on $\mathcal M^n imes [0, au ]$, hence $u\ge 0$ there as well. As $ au $ was arbitrary, the result follows.

□
